chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Rifa'a who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who commits fornication before he consummates his marriage — is he stoned? He said: No.

key_terms.إِحْصَان: the legal status of being 'married with consummation' that activates the stoning penalty
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِأَهْلِهِ: consummation of marriage — entering upon one's wife in the marital sense
key_terms.يَزْنِي: commits fornication/adultery (zina) — sexual intercourse outside of lawful marriage
key_terms.يُرْجَمُ: stoning (rajm) — the hadd punishment for zina by a muhsan (married, consummating) person

ai.seo_question: Is a man who commits zina (fornication) before consummating his marriage subject to stoning (rajm) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the Islamic penal ruling for a man who commits fornication (zina) before consummating his marriage. The Imam's concise answer — 'No' — establishes that such a man does not incur the hadd punishment of stoning (rajm), since the legal prerequisite of ihsan (confirmed marital status through consummation) has not been fulfilled. In classical Shia fiqh, the death penalty by stoning for zina applies specifically to the muhsan — one who has consummated a valid marriage — not to one who has merely contracted it.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Rafa’at who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who commited adultery before he copulated with his wife, would he be stoned?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
